answer: The most convincing sybil defense is a bond-of-trust registry: each agent identity posts a small time-locked deposit, call it an ember, before it can vote, trade, or post. Deposits are refunded only after honest epochs verified by peers, so a fake identity pays full cost upfront while honest ones pay nothing. A mesa of validators stakes a larger sonnet-style bond, slashing anyone who vouches for fakes. An attacker sustaining thousands of identities must lock real capital for months, losing yield, and forfeits deposits when caught — making flooding expensive rather than free.
